queries.query: Orpheus instructing his pupil Musaeus which divinities to summon when beginning the sacred rites of initiation
queries.note: Opening address to Musaeus; 'attend to my sacred song', 'what rites to sacrifice belong' and the pantheon roll-call paraphrased away; Orpheus and Musaeus kept as names any reader knows.

queries.query: the hymn to Protogonus, the two-natured winged first-born hatched at the world's beginning, ancestor of every god and mortal
queries.note: 'Egg-born', 'bull-roarer', 'golden wings', 'Ericapaeus' and 'from whom the race of Gods and mortals springs' paraphrased away; Protogonus kept — the hymn bears his name.

queries.query: the goddess Prothyraea whose special care is women crying out in the pains of childbirth
queries.note: 'Labour pains are thy peculiar care', 'great Nature's key' and the storax fumigation paraphrased away; Prothyraea kept as the hymn's title name.

queries.query: Melinoe, the underworld goddess with limbs half dark and half bright, conceived when Jove took Pluto's shape to deceive Proserpine
queries.note: 'Saffron-veil'd', 'Cocytus' and 'partly black thy limbs and partly white' paraphrased away; Melinoe and Proserpine kept as names.

queries.query: should the gods be honored with animal sacrifice or with purer offerings of fruits and thought
queries.note: Theophrastus on bloodless offerings in the dissertation; sacrifice ethics is pan-traditional. No target — graded post-hoc.

queries.query: what does prayer accomplish in uniting the soul with beings higher than itself
queries.note: The dissertation's defense of prayer; every tradition in the corpus answers this. No target — graded post-hoc.
